mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, exalted is He, {جَاعل الْمَلَائِكَة رسلًا}: tanwīn on جاعل is not permissible because it is for the past, and رسلا is a second object. It is also said that it is accusative by an implied verb, because an active participle with a past meaning does not govern in the accusative.
His saying {مثنى وَثَلَاث وَربَاع}: these are numbers diverted (maʿdūla) while indefinite, and they became definite by the diversion; so they are diptotes because of the diversion and definiteness. It is also said: because of the diversion and being adjectives. The benefit of the diversion is that they indicate repetition: the meaning of مثنى is "two by two", ثلاث "three by three", and likewise رباع. The explanation of this has already been given at the beginning of al-Nisāʾ.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying {غير الله}: whoever reads غير in the nominative makes it an agent, as you say هل ضارب غير زيد, meaning "except Zayd". It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of خلق according to its position. The accusative is permissible by exception. Whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a naʿt of خلق according to its wording.
[Translator's note: the source has «نعت الخلق» and «نعتا لخلق», while the verse reads {هَلْ مِنْ خَالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ}; خالق is evidently meant. Both are translated as written.]

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying {بِاللَّه الْغرُور}: whoever reads the ghayn with fatḥa makes it a name for Satan; whoever reads it with ḍamma makes it the plural of غارّ ("deceiver"), like your saying جالس and جلوس. It is also said that it is the plural of غَرّ, and غَرّ is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also said that it is a maṣdar, like الدخول.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying {الَّذين كفرُوا لَهُم عَذَاب}: الذين is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for أصحاب, or in the position of the accusative as a badal for حزبه, or in the position of the nominative as a badal for the latent pronoun in ليكونوا.
His saying {وَالَّذين آمنُوا}: الذين is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); مغفرة is a second mubtadaʾ, لهم is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar about الذين.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t:
His saying {حسرات}: accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
The hāʾ in يرفعه refers to الكلم; it is also said that it refers to العمل. So on the second view the accusative is permissible in العمل by an implied verb which يرفعه explains, while on the first view only the nominative is permissible.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {يمكرون السَّيِّئَات}: السيئات is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because يمكرون means "they do evil". It is also said that its implied form is "they plot the evil plots", then the described noun was omitted. It is also said that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with يمكرون meaning "they do".

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {وَلَو كَانَ ذَا قربى}: the ism (noun) of كان is latent in it, its implied form being "even if the one called were a relative". In ordinary speech ولو كان ذو قربى is permissible, with كان meaning "occurred", or with the khabar (predicate) omitted.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying {مُخْتَلف ألوانه}: i.e. "creatures whose colours are different"; the hāʾ refers to the omitted noun. مختلف is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the genitive phrase before it is its khabar (predicate), and ألوانه is an agent.
His saying {كَذَلِك إِنَّمَا يخْشَى الله من عباده الْعلمَاء}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a difference like that difference mentioned before".

mekki-muskil:33-33.t:
His saying {أساور}: the plural of أسورة, and أسورة is the plural of سوار and سُوار; إسوار has been reported for the singular, and its plural is أساوير.
His saying {جنَّات عدن}: the nominative in جنات is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with يدخلونها as the khabar (predicate), or by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are gardens", with يدخلونها a naʿt (adjective) of جنات.
His saying {يحلونَ فِيهَا} and {ولباسهم فِيهَا حَرِير}: both are adjectives of جنات, whether you put it in the nominative or in the accusative as a badal (substitute) for الخيرات or by an implied verb that what follows explains. They may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun, referring to the nominative (pronoun) in يدخلونها, because in each of the two aḥwāl there are two returning pronouns, one referring to the nominative (pronoun) in يدخلونها and the other to the accusative.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {الَّذِي أحلنا}: الذي is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of the ism (noun) of إنّ, or in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, or as a badal (substitute) for غفور, or as a badal for the latent pronoun in شكور.
His saying {دَار المقامة}: المقامة means "residence" (الإقامة).

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {أَن تَزُولَا}: أن is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "lest they cease". It is also said that its meaning is "from ceasing" (من أن تزولا), because the meaning of يمسك is "prevents".

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying {استكبارا}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
His saying {ومكر السيء}: this is the annexation of the described noun to its adjective, and its implied form is "and they plotted the evil plot"; the evidence for it is His saying, exalted is He, after that, ولا يحيق المكر السيء إلا بأهله. So مكر السيء is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and then it was annexed to its adjective by extension, like صلاة الأولى and مسجد الجامع.

mekki-muskil:45-45.t: His saying {فَإِذا جَاءَ أَجلهم}: بصيرا may not govern إذا, because what comes after إنّ does not govern what precedes it: if you said اليوم إن زيدا خارج, putting اليوم in the accusative by خارج, it would not be permissible. Rather its governor is جاء, because إذا has the meaning of a conditional requital (jazāʾ), and the nouns used for conditional requital are governed by what follows them: you say من أكرم يكرمني, and أكرم is the governor of من without disagreement. So إذا resembled the conditional particles because of the meaning of condition in it, and what follows it governed it. Its due would have been not to be governed by it, because it is annexed to the clauses that follow it; there is disagreement about whether this is permissible, and there is room for consideration in it, because according to Sībawayh إذا is not used for conditional requital except in poetry. So in the place where it is used for conditional requital, the verb that follows it can govern it, just as it governs ما and من, which are for condition; and in the place where it is not used for conditional requital, it is not good for the verb that follows it to govern it, because it is annexed to the clause after it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf, since it is part of its completion, just as a thing does not govern itself. There is disagreement about the implied annexation of إذا.
